title: Pointwise Competing-Risk CATE Rates under Censoring in Observational and Randomized Designs
banked_reason: D0.5 math panel passed, but D0.5.G graded subfield below the fixed field floor with paper score ceiling 7.2 < 7.4 and no bounded in-scope repair.
gap_reasons: The exact n^-r frontier is confined to known-uniform-design, fixed-K classes under cubic negligibility; the strict cubic-active phase remains bracketed.
Broader design, adaptive tuning, inference, and numerical evidence are absent.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived an observable second-order correction, a correlated-sign full-history lower experiment, and a matched pointwise rate on known-uniform-design, fixed-K classes where the cubic pilot term is negligible. The math panel passed and verified the Lei source, but the general reviewer graded the finished scope subfield below the field floor. The strict cubic-active phase remains bracketed, and deleting a stale randomized-wedge dependency marked one proof closure stale in the graph despite preserved proof text.
tldr: For the known-uniform-design, fixed-horizon competing-risk experiment, the paper proves a same-class pointwise frontier at the full exponent \(r\): mixed-scale second-order correction governs below the elbow and ordinary pointwise localization governs at saturation, subject only to the declared cubic-negligibility condition.  The randomized class with known Bernoulli assignment has the analogous full exponent \(r_{\mathrm{rand}}\), including its saturation branch; unknown retention slows the concrete \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\eta=\beta_1=\beta_2=0.12\) configuration to \(12/43\), while known assignment and retention give \(1/3\).  At \(L=\varepsilon\), the contrast and all corresponding minimax risks are exactly zero.
gap: Competing-risk CATE papers provide identifying transformations, learner comparisons, and generic oracle inequalities, while the sharp Hölder theory covers uncensored CATEs; the intersection has no verified same-class pointwise minimax frontier.
fill: The project pairs a pilot-weighted projected U-statistic correction with a full-support correlated-sign mixture whose shared-sign components yield the matching Hellinger order.
